subgroups.name: solve 1

steps.hints:
❓Which tiles should be set as walls? 

❓Which tiles should not be set as walls, so that sprites are able to overlap them?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja: 

❓ Which tiles will a sprite be unable to overlap? Why?


Solution: 

The walls on all of the lava tiles should be erased in the tilemap editor.


(see tilemap solution below)
steps.instructions:
When the Player sprite falls into the lava, nothing happens!


Fix the bugs in the tilemap so that the camera shakes, a sound is played, and the Player sprite returns to its starting position when overlapping a lava tile.

subgroups.introduction:
Oh no - these programs aren’t working! Problems in code are called bugs. Find and fix the bugs in the code in each section!


Fix the bugs in the code so that the Player sprite is able to jump to collect enough Food sprites to win the game, while also avoiding obstacle tiles.

validationItems.text: Walls should be disabled on all lava tiles in the tilemap editor.
validationItems.failureText: Check to see whether the Player sprite is able  to overlap with the lava tile.

subgroups.name: solve 2

steps.hints: ❓Would the vy (velocity y) value need to be increased or decreased for the sprite to jump higher?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja: 

❓ Which value affects how high the Player sprite is able to jump?


Solution: 

The value in the [set sprite vy (velocity y)] block should be decreased (likely near -200 or -250).
steps.instructions:
When the A button is pressed, the Player sprite is not able to reach the platform.


Fix the bugs in the code so that when the A button is pressed, the Player sprite jumps high enough to reach the platform.

When the Player sprite reaches the magic portal tile, the game does not end even if the Player sprite has collected all of the coins on the tilemap.


Fix the bugs in the code so that there are enough coins spawning on the tilemap for the Player sprite to collect, in order to win the game.

})

    otherSprite.destroy(effects.rings, 500)
    info.changeScoreBy(1)

    } else {
        game.showLongText("Collect 5 stars to open the magical portal!", DialogLayout.Center)

subgroups.introduction:
Oh no - these programs aren’t working! Problems in code are called bugs. Find and fix the bugs in the code in each section!


Fix the bugs in the code so that the Player sprite is able to jump to collect enough Food sprites to win the game, while also avoiding obstacle tiles.

validationItems.text: 1-2 yellow squares are added to the tilemap, where a coin will be placed.
validationItems.failureText: Check the number of spawn tiles where coin sprites will be placed in the tilemap editor.

attributes.description: Welcome to Level 1 of Green Belt! In this level, you’ll learn more about 2D platformer games and physics. In 2D platformers, we see the game as if looking from the side. We can use physics concepts, like velocity and acceleration, to make our sprites jump up onto platforms and avoid obstacles. Here are the achievements you’ll unlock in Level 1:

badges.title: Let’s Get Physics-cal!
badges.description: Use physics to control sprite movement in a platformer-style tilemap project.

badges.title: Hop, Skip, and a Jump
badges.description: Set a sprite’s y-velocity (vy).

badges.title: Defying Gravity
badges.description: Set a sprite’s y-acceleration (ay).

badges.title: Wallflower
badges.description: Check if a sprite is touching a tilemap wall before making something happen in a project.
